text:
The suspect should be found not guilty if the jury believes his account, because the statute forbids force used only to resist a known arrest and still allows reasonable self-defense against an officer’s excessive force, and a punch to stop an unprovoked nightstick beating fits that privilege. He should be found guilty if the jury believes the officer, because that account has him striking first to resist arrest. The lawfulness of the arrest, including probable cause, is immaterial under either account.

CONFIDENCE: 86
